intro.title: Controlled vs Uncontrolled
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple form with two input fields to explore controlled and uncontrolled components in React. You'll learn how controlled components manage form data through React state, while uncontrolled components rely on the DOM directly. The core programming concepts include using React state with the useState hook, handling events like onChange, and accessing DOM elements via refs. By the end, you'll understand when to use each approach and implement both in a functional React component.
intro.usecase: Controlled vs uncontrolled components is a fundamental React pattern that appears in nearly every interactive UI. In real software products, controlled components are essential for forms where you need instant validation and feedback—like login screens that show password requirements as you type. Uncontrolled components work well for simple inputs where you only need the final value, such as search filters that submit on enter or file upload inputs. Understanding when to use each approach helps developers build more efficient dashboards, settings panels, and data entry interfaces with appropriate state management.
